children: Sterling falls after data showed continued signs of softness in the U.K. labor market ahead of Thursday's Bank of England interest-rate decision. The unemployment rate held at 4.9% in the three months to July, as expected by economists in a WSJ survey. The number of payrolled employees dropped by 39,000 over the quarter. "A still sluggish labor market will give the Bank some confidence that Bank Rate remains restrictive," Deutsche Bank's Sanjay Raja says in a note. Sterling falls 0.2% to an intraday low of $1.3461 after the data, from $1.3479 beforehand. The euro rises 0.1% to an intraday high of 0.8562 pounds, from 0.8556 previously. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
